sketches.title: Meeting Chain
sketches.premise: You and your opponent build a workday meeting chain. On your turn, add one office event that directly causes, fixes, or replaces the event just named; the chain ends when an event cannot sensibly handle the one before it.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new standing event acts on the previous event in a plain office way; merely waiting it out, avoiding it, making a bigger copy, or naming a close cousin without an effect loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I call a meeting about the meeting, because the first meeting created a decision nobody understood." The host notes that the meeting has now reproduced, which is not the same as solving anything.
sketches.first_card: A meeting starts five minutes late.

sketches.title: Desk Dispatch
sketches.premise: Your desk is a tiny office town, and each turn sends one everyday office object to deal with the object just placed. The object must physically use, block, remove, or change the previous one, so the desk becomes a chain of practical little rescues.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts a clear physical office action such as a lid closing a box or a bin taking paper, but rejects hiding, surviving, a larger version of the same object, and a related object that does nothing to the one before it.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am a paperclip, pinning the loose note to the board." The host observes that the note has finally been promoted from wandering around to having one job.
sketches.first_card: A loose sheet of paper lies on the desk.

sketches.title: Inbox Tetris
sketches.premise: You and your opponent manage a shared office inbox one message at a time. Each new message must directly resolve, redirect, or make an answerable decision from the message before it; one useless reply collapses the inbox.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a concrete reply action on the standing message; ignoring it, postponing it, saying the same request more loudly, or changing to a nearby topic without handling it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I reply, ‘Approved—please send the file,’ turning the request for approval into the next clear task." The host says the inbox has achieved the rare dignity of moving forward.
sketches.first_card: “Can you approve this?” arrives with a file attached.

sketches.title: Office Weather
sketches.premise: The office has weather made from ordinary work events: a cold draft, a paper storm, a bright window, a coffee flood. Each turn introduces a new office condition that directly changes or ends the condition just described.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new condition acts on the previous one by blocking, stopping, soaking, warming, or otherwise changing it; simply sheltering from it, enduring it, or making a stronger version loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am a closed window, stopping the cold draft from crossing the room." The host reports that the draft has been defeated by the ancient technology of shutting something.
sketches.first_card: A cold draft moves through the open-plan office.

sketches.title: Calendar Court
sketches.premise: Your calendar is a courtroom, and each turn presents one office appointment that must directly overrule, fit, or repair the appointment before it. The appointments are standing commitments, so the Judge cares about what the new one does to the old one, not about a story of what happened earlier.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts a clear calendar action such as cancelling, moving, shortening, or replacing the prior appointment, but rejects double-booking, merely attending both, a longer version of the same appointment, or an appointment from the same kind of meeting that changes nothing.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am a rescheduled meeting, moving the budget review to the empty hour and freeing this slot." The host notes that the calendar has discovered moving a problem is different from inviting a second problem.
sketches.first_card: A team meeting is booked during your only lunch break.

sketches.title: Printer Rescue
sketches.premise: You and your opponent keep an office printer working by naming one ordinary thing that directly fixes or defeats the printer problem just named. Every move must be a practical tool, supply, setting, or person that acts on the standing problem; when one fails, the printer wins.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a direct repair, clearing, supplying, or control action; waiting, trying the same fix in a larger form, choosing a related office item that cannot act, or merely avoiding the printer loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am a paper tray, giving the empty printer pages to pull." The host remarks that this is a bold strategy: supplying paper to a printer that had the nerve to ask for paper.
